node_definition.done_when: Read section 36 of crew-runtime-positive-controls first. In reckon/crew/promotion.py, the accept-path claim check (reached through _landing_gate and _accepted_scope_exceptions) accepts a path whose change by this run is already reachable from the integration head, even while another live run claims it. It leaves the peer's claim and pointer untouched, and records on the acceptance that the path was already integrated, naming the peer claims present. A path whose change is not on the integration head is still refused on a live claim. tests/test_integrated_companion_path_is_accepted.py, in a temporary git repository and RECKON_HOME, covers both cases and asserts the peer pointer is byte-for-byte unchanged. Existing promotion tests that reach _accepted_scope_exceptions keep passing; grep tests/ for it and for accept-path to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/integrated-companion-path-is-accepted.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
